question: As per September 2024, according to the Ministry of External Affairs in India, there are ______ million Indians residing abroad who are either NRIs or OCIs.
solution:
The correct answer is __**32 million**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• As per the data released by the **Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), India**, in **September 2024**, the estimated number of **Indians residing abroad**, including **Non-Resident Indians (NRIs)** and **Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs)**, is approximately **32 million**.

• This includes Indians living in countries across continents such as the **United States, the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia**, and other nations.

• The figure represents a mix of Indians who have either migrated for work, education, or permanent settlement and those who maintain Indian citizenship but reside abroad temporarily.

• The MEA consistently updates this figure through consultations with embassies, consulates, and official surveys conducted worldwide.

• These individuals contribute significantly to India’s **economy** through **remittances**, which stood at a record high of **$111 billion in 2023**, making India the world’s largest recipient of remittances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Non-Resident Indians (NRIs):**

• An **NRI** is an Indian citizen who resides outside India for employment, education, or other purposes for an indefinite period.

• NRIs retain their Indian citizenship but are typically subject to specific tax regulations under the **Income Tax Act, 1961**.

• They contribute significantly to the Indian economy through **foreign direct investments (FDIs)** and remittances.

• **Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs):**

• OCIs are individuals of Indian origin who hold citizenship in another country but are granted certain privileges in India, such as **visa-free travel** and the ability to own property.

• The **OCI card** was introduced under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2005, to strengthen ties between India and its diaspora.

• OCIs are not allowed to vote or hold constitutional office in India.

• **Indian Diaspora:**

• The Indian diaspora is the **largest in the world**, with members spread across **more than 200 countries**.

• Key regions of settlement include the **Middle East** (especially GCC countries), **North America, Europe, and Southeast Asia**.

• They are known for their contributions to local economies and their role in enhancing **India’s soft power** globally.

• **Remittances to India:**

• India received a record **$111 billion** in remittances in **2023**, accounting for approximately **3% of its GDP**.

• The major sources of remittances include the **United States, UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the UK**.

• This financial inflow helps India maintain a stable **current account balance** and supports rural households significantly.

• **MEA Initiatives for Indians Abroad:**

• The **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas**, celebrated annually, recognizes the contributions of the Indian diaspora to India’s development.

• The **e-Migrate system** ensures the safety and welfare of Indian workers migrating to other countries for employment.

• The **Vande Bharat Mission** was launched to repatriate Indians stranded abroad during the COVID-19 pandemic.
